sources.title: NGSS 4-LS1-2: Use a model to describe that animals receive different types of information through their senses, process the information in their brain, and respond to the information in different ways
OpenStax Biology 2e, 36.4 Hearing and Vestibular Sensation
OpenStax Biology 2e, 38.1 Types of Skeletal Systems (the smallest bones)

note.text: Your ears take in information about the world as sound. The outer ear's shape helps collect sound and funnel it in.

steps.title: Ear canal
steps.instruction: Draw both sides of the ear canal.

note.text: Sound travels down the ear canal, a short tunnel into your head.

steps.title: Eardrum
steps.instruction: Trace the eardrum at the end of the canal.

note.text: The eardrum is a thin sheet stretched across the canal. Sound makes it vibrate, like the skin of a drum.

steps.title: Ear bones
steps.instruction: Trace the three tiny ear bones.

note.text: The hammer, anvil and stirrup pass the eardrum's vibrations inward. They're the smallest bones in your body.
The cochlea is filled with fluid. It turns the vibrations into signals your nerves can carry.

steps.title: Hearing nerve
steps.instruction: Draw the nerve to the brain.

note.text: A nerve carries the signals from the cochlea to your brain.
Your brain works out what the sound is, like a voice or a bell, and decides how you'll respond.

steps.title: Sound
steps.instruction: Draw the arrow of sound coming in.

note.text: Sound is made by vibrations that travel through the air to your ear.

steps.title: From sound to brain
steps.instruction: Tap the parts in the order sound and its signals reach them.
steps.why: The outer ear collects sound, it travels down the canal, shakes the eardrum and ear bones, the cochlea turns it into signals, and a nerve carries them to the brain.
steps.hint: Which part catches the sound first?

steps.title: Respond
steps.question: A friend calls your name from behind you, and you turn around. What happened?

options.text: Your ears took in the sound, your brain recognized your name, and it told your body to turn
options.feedback: Yes. Senses gather information, the brain makes sense of it, and then you respond.
Ears only gather sound. Your brain decides to turn, and your muscles do it.
Eyes sense light. Sound is sensed by your ears, then your brain decides.

options.text: The sound pushed your head around
options.feedback: Sound is too gentle for that. Your brain recognized your name and chose to turn.
